result.topic_en: Series expansions relating a variable x to an angle φ (via theta-like series 2x^{1/4}+2x^{9/4}, 1+4x+4xx) and derivation of a second-order differential equation for a function Q(φ), with P and Q satisfying PQ'+QP' = 2/(π sin 2φ), in connection with the arithmetic-geometric mean.
result.transcription:
$2x^{\frac14}+2x^{\frac94}$
$4x^{\frac12}+8x^{\frac52}\ldots$
$1+4x+4xx$
$\frac{\pi}{\log x \quad 1+4x}$
$\frac{\log x.(1+4x+4xx\ldots)}{\pi}$

$\frac{9^6}{26.60}$ $\frac{32}{.720}$

$4x^{\frac12}(1-4x+14xx) = \varphi-\frac16\varphi^3+\frac1{120}\varphi^5$
$16x(1-8x+44xx) = \varphi^2-\frac13\varphi^4+\frac2{45}\varphi^6$
$128xx = \frac1{4}\varphi^4$
$x = \frac1{16}\varphi^2+\frac1{96}\varphi^4+$

$+\frac1{64}\varphi^4$
$2\log\varphi+\log\frac1{16}$ $\quad 1+\frac14\varphi\varphi+\frac{11}{192}\varphi^4$

$P\varphi = \frac{2\log\varphi+1+\frac5{12}\varphi\varphi+\quad-\log 16}{\pi}$
$Q\varphi = \frac{\frac2\varphi+\frac56\varphi+}{\pi}$
$Qs = \frac{\alpha}{s}+6s+\gamma s^3\ldots$

$Q'' = Q(1+\frac{4}{[-2\sin 2\varphi-]\sin 2\varphi^2})+[-\frac{2Q'}{\sin}-]+2\cot 2\varphi.Q'$
$\frac{ddQ}{d\varphi^2}-\frac{dQ}{d\varphi}\frac{dd\varphi}{d\varphi^2} = Q(1+\frac{4}{ss})+2c\frac{dQ}{d\varphi}$
$d\varphi = \frac{dx}{\cos\varphi}$
$dd\varphi = \frac{\sin\varphi dx}{\cos\varphi^2}$

$PQ'+QP' = \frac{2}{\pi\sin 2\varphi}$
$\frac{\log x}{\pi}$ 0

$\frac{Q''}{c}-\frac{Q's}{cc} = Q(1+\frac4{ss})\frac1{c^3}+\frac{2c}{ccs}Q'$
$\frac{Q''}{c}-Q'\frac{(ss-2cc)}{ccs} = Q(1+\frac4{ss})\frac1{c^3}$
$Q''cs-Q'$

methods.what: Series expansions of theta-like functions in x
Equating series in x with sine series in φ
Squared relation equated with sin^2 series
Series reversion giving x as power series in φ
Expansion of P(φ) with logarithmic term
Second-order differential equation for Q in φ
Change of variables in the differential equation
Wronskian-type relation between P and Q
